LESSON: INTERNAL LAND FORMING PROCESSES • RIFT VALLEY • BLOCK MOUNTAIN • FAULTS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.2: Internal Land Forming Processes • Rift valley • Block mountain • Faults
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Internal Land Forming Processes • Rift valley • Block mountain • Faults, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How do landforms influence human activities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Internal Land Forming Processes • Rift valley • Block mountain • Faults together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: learners use relevant digital resources as they watch video clips/documentaries on the processes of faulting in

the environment.

• Learning to Learn: learners build on their own learning experiences as they conduct library research on types of faults in the

environment and do a presentation in class.

Values:
• Respect: learners brainstorm in groups on the types and causes of earth movements and present them in class.

• Responsibility: learners take care of their property and those of others as they use digital or print resources to research

theories of continental drift and plate tectonics in the environment and make short notes.

Pertinent Contemporary Issues (PCIs):

• Environmental education: learners discuss and share in class the significance of faulting in human activities.

• Disaster risk reduction: learners address disaster risk reduction as they develop posters to create awareness of disasters

relating to faulting.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Learners apply Kenyan Sign Language, English, and Kiswahili language skills as they brainstorm the types and causes of

earth movements.

• Learners use Agriculture knowledge to discuss and share in class the significance of faulting in human activities.
